title: Seeded range-bound pruning for the exact GPU range scorer
status: protocol registered 2026-11-17; no recorded run yet
question: Does seeded range-bound pruning make the exact GPU range scorer faster on the full collection, and how much of any change comes from the range size, the work-list scheduling and the pruning itself?
hypothesis: Pruning scores far fewer postings and ranges, so the pruned scorer is faster than the exhaustive control, more so at smaller ranges; per-query overhead limits the gain.
motivation: The range scorer is exhaustive; the project's safe-block-bound idea was tested only on the older CSR layout. A development census shows that at 64 seeds only 22-65% of postings need scoring, depending on range size.

declared_changes.new_inputs: range-size 512 and 256 indexes built from the pinned GSP with the unchanged builder, pinned by SHA-256

correctness_rule: Every configuration's ordered (original_id, score) top-10 equals the pinned CPU reference for every query, in correctness and in every timing process; the seeds-64 configurations' schedules equal the host recomputation on every query.
success_rule: A complete run under the registered protocol; the result is reported whatever the speedups are.
failure_rule: Any mismatch, rejected expected run, failure other than a contended GPU failure, or more than 3 ineligible processes for one configuration.
